units: <cite ref="Bekhorot 8a:13">Bekh. 8ᵃ</cite> <he>הפיל והק׳ והקיפוף וכ׳</he> the elephant, the ape, and the long-tailed ape (cercopithacos) give birth after three years of pregnancy.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 58a:6">B. Bath. 58ᵃ</cite> <he>כק׳ בפני אדם</he> as inferior in looks as the ape is to man.

<cite ref="Yoma 29b:6">Yoma 29ᵇ</cite> <he>כמו שסדרו הק׳</he> as if an ape had arranged it on the table (as an unconscious act). Tanḥ. P’ḳudé 3; a. e.—[<cite ref="Mishnah Parah 3:5">Par. III, 5</cite> <he>בן הקוף</he>, Mish. ed., v. <cite ref="S01093"><he>קַיָּף</he></cite>.]—Pl. <he>קוֹפִים</he>, <he>קוֹפִין</he>, <he>קוֹפוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 80a">B. Kam. 80ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 8:17">Tosef. ib. VIII, 17</cite>.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 109a:5">Snh. 109ᵃ</cite> <he>נעשו ק׳ ורוחות וכ׳</he> were turned into apes, spirits, demons and night-demons.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 23:6">Gen. R. s. 23</cite> (in the days of Enosh) <he>נעשו … כק׳</he> men’s faces were made to be ape-like.

<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 6:11:1">Koh. R. to VI, 11</cite> (ref. to <he>מרבים הבל</he>, <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 6:11:1">ib.</cite>) <he>כגון מגדלי ק׳ וכ׳</he> as those who rear apes, cats &c.; a. e.
